points.text: States that DNA is transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus
Explains that the mRNA is translated into a polypeptide at a ribosome in the cytoplasm

items.prompt: Outline the central dogma in one or two sentences, naming where transcription and translation happen.

points.text: States that a son has only one X chromosome, so the recessive h allele has no second allele to mask it and the trait shows
Explains that a daughter has a second X carrying H, which masks h, so she is a carrier without symptoms

items.prompt: A carrier mother (X^H X^h) and a normal father (X^H Y) have children. Explain why a son who inherits X^h has haemophilia, while a daughter who inherits X^h usually does not.

points.text: States that chloroplasts trap light energy to make sugar in photosynthesis
Explains that mitochondria release energy from that sugar as ATP in aerobic respiration, which continues day and night

items.prompt: A leaf cell contains both chloroplasts and mitochondria. Explain, in terms of photosynthesis and respiration, why it needs both.

points.text: States a phospholipid bilayer with hydrophilic heads facing outward and hydrophobic tails inside, with proteins drifting through it
Explains that channel proteins allow only selected substances to cross

items.prompt: Describe the structure of the cell membrane in the fluid mosaic model and explain how that structure makes it selectively permeable.

levels.descriptor: Methods are chosen and applied exactly, central dogma steps and cross ratios are stated explicitly, sex-linked reasoning names the single X in sons, cell membrane structure is described with heads, tails and channel proteins, and conclusions are justified without claiming every mutation harms the organism.
levels.label: Secure

levels.descriptor: Method is correct in outline but a central dogma step, cross ratio, sex-linked step or membrane step is skipped.
levels.label: Developing

levels.descriptor: Methods are misapplied - for example claiming every mutation harms the organism because any change to DNA breaks a protein - and the working does not support the answer.
levels.label: Beginning
